name: Pye
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Pai (Nigeria, Plateau): only wordlists (Blench 2023/2006, Williamson 1973) per Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description; no grammar or phonology

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2023. The Pe language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Circulation draft, May 27, 2023. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 27 pp. (academia.edu 102454393; full text layer read from the Internet Archive copy of the academia page)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 3.3 Tones p. 5: 'The tone system of Pe is not well recorded, but it can be assumed to be similar to Tarok with three level tones and rising and falling.' Phonology otherwise = vowels, consonants, palatalisation/labialisation, homorganic nasals.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Yakubu Danladi, Julius Dabet, Benard Abraham & Innocent Jonah. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Pye (Pe) [pai] Language of Plateau State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-004. Dallas: SIL International. 48 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.2 Phonology pp. 10-11: consonant and vowel inventories from a 348-item wordlist; 'there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological features, nor has there been an effort to determine the phonemic status of phones'. Wordlist (App. E) marks some tones, no stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The Pe language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment (printout April 25, 2006). Cambridge: Mallam Dendo. ii+24 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology (pp. 4-5) gives a six-vowel inventory, consonant chart, VV sequences and homorganic nasals; heading '3.3 Tones' is empty; intro p. 2: 'In general, tones are not marked'. No mention of stress or accent anywhere.
